subject: Retrieve raw copy numbers and snp IDs

messages.author: 730676538d6f7c91
messages.subject: Retrieve raw copy numbers and snp IDs
parts:
Hi there,

I am new in using adorma.affymetrix package and just got a problem to
receive raw copy numbers for all samples. It seems that
extractRawCopyNumbers only returns the copy numbers of a particular
array and chromosome. Is there anyway to return raw copy numbers of
multiple samples on all of chromosomes? Also can I get Affy SNP IDs
instead of unit ids?

Thanks!
Jeff

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Retrieve raw copy numbers and snp IDs
parts:
On Mon, Aug 18, 2008 at 10:15 AM, Jeff <blue...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi there,
>
> I am new in using adorma.affymetrix package and just got a problem to
> receive raw copy numbers for all samples. It seems that
> extractRawCopyNumbers only returns the copy numbers of a particular
> array and chromosome. Is there anyway to return raw copy numbers of
> multiple samples on all of chromosomes?

It is not clear what format such data should be in, but yes,
extractRawCopyNumbers() is array and chromosome specific. You can of
course call it for all chromosomes and arrays and merge the data
together yourself. However, you find the approach explained in the
online Vignette 'Calculating raw total copy numbers manually'
[http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calculating-raw-total-copy-numbers-manually]
more useful.
> Also can I get Affy SNP IDs instead of unit ids?

When you say "unit ids", do you mean unit indices, because to me the
unit IDs are the same as "Affy SNP IDs". So, if you have a vector of
unit indices, then you can use getUnitNames() of AffymetrixCdfFile to
retrieve the corresponding unit names (a.k.a. unit IDs, "Affy SNP
IDs", ...). Example:

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6,Full");
> units <- c(1:5, 1002:1008, 1020512);
> unitNames <- getUnitNames(cdf, units=units);
> unitNames
[1] "AFFX-5Q-123" "AFFX-5Q-456" "AFFX-5Q-789" "AFFX-5Q-ABC"
[5] "AFR_A02_SB" "SNP_A-2001454" "SNP_A-2001478" "SNP_A-2001480"
[9] "SNP_A-2001481" "SNP_A-2001483" "SNP_A-2001522" "SNP_A-4214089"
[13] "CN_846076"

This is also illustrated in the above vignette. In addition to use
the extractMatrix() function mention in that vignette, you should also
know about extractDataFrame(). I think the latter is illustrated
further in the exon vignette and has been mentions in the mailing list
(see the archive).

Hope this helps you get started

Henrik
